 Virtual vs real exercise

Senior science writer


 Can video games be sports? The Esports Foundation, a Saudi Arabian non-profit outfit, thinks so: in July and August it hosted the 2026 Esports World Cup in Paris, in which competitors played everything from driving games and first-person shooters to, er, chess, for a share of a $75m prize purse.


 Grumpy traditionalists might disagree: after all, playing video games involves little more physical effort than clicking a button. But that is not quite true.
